abstract:
Let $m\ge 3$ be odd and let $S=\mathbf{P}^1_\lambda\setminus\{0,\infty,1,-1\}\subset\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$ be the one-dimensional symmetric slice of degree-$m$ cyclic covers $C_\lambda	o\mathbf{P}^1$ branched at $(-1,-\lambda,0,\lambda,1,\infty)$ with a $(2,2,1,1)$-symmetric weight tuple $\mathbf{a}$ under an involution $h\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ ($H=\{1,h\}$). Unlike on $\mathcal{M}_{0,6}$, under the local non-resonance conditions of Lemma 2.1 (satisfied by all units $t\in(\mathbf{Z}/m\mathbf{Z})^	imes$ on our CRT families), every puncture of $S$ is a simultaneous multi-point collision whose local monodromy generator $g_p(t)$ ($p\in\{1,-1,0,\infty\}$) on $V_t=H_1(C_\lambda,\mathbf{C})_t$ and non-scalar powers $g_p(t)^k
otin\mathbf{C}^	imes I_4$ have $\operatorname{rank}(g_p(t)^k-cI_4)\ge 2$ for all $c\in\mathbf{C}^	imes$, excluding rank-$1$ pseudoreflections and transvections; moreover, for composite $m=a\cdot m'$ ($\gcd(a,m')=1$), the multiplier $v\equiv(-1,+1)\pmod{(a,m')}
otin\pm H$ is locally isospectral with $t=1$ and collides on the length-$2$ braid words $g_1g_0$ and $g_1g_{-1}$.

We establish an unconditional global braid-monodromy rigidity and cyclotomic separation theory on $S$: (1) cyclotomic linear disjointness in the $g_1(t)$-eigenbasis yields the adjoint dichotomy $\mathfrak{g}\in\{\{0\},\mathfrak{sl}_4(\mathbf{C})\}$ (Theorem A); (2) for $m=15N$ ($\gcd(N,30)=1$), Ramanujan-sum trace averages of $(g_1g_0)^2$ prove factorwise Zariski density in $\operatorname{SU}(J(t))$ up to $\mu_{15N}$ scalars, and dual-basis expansion of $g_1^2g_0$ over $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_N)$ separates all non-trivial cosets $[t]
eq[\pm 1]$ (Theorem B); (3) $g_1^2g_0$ uniformly separates $v$ from $\pm H$ for coprime odd $a,m'\ge 3$ (Theorem C); and (4) Galois involution projections extend density and length-$3$ separation to three-factor conductors $m=a\cdot b\cdot N$ ($\gcd(N,30)=1$), alongside four method-boundary examples (Theorem D). By Goursat's lemma, this determines the generic derived Mumford–Tate group $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})_{\mathrm{der}}=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(J(t))$ and endomorphism algebra $\mathbf{Q}(\zeta_m)^H$, and on characterwise $(2,2)$-balanced subfamilies ($d_t=3$) gives $\operatorname{Hg}(B_{\eta,\mathrm{prim}})=\prod_{[t]}\operatorname{SU}(2,2)$, reducing all-powers Hodge algebraicity to the separate determinant-cycle input on individual factors (Corollary E).
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Section 7 opening paragraph & Section 1.2 (Theorem D summary): Aligned the overview of the four method-boundary examples (b.1)-(b.4) with the precise distinction in Section 7.3, distinguishing the companion-template examples (b.1) at (9, 5, 7) and (b.2) at (3, 7, 11) (admissible coprime parameter triples outside the generalized primary family (1.9)) from the generalized primary family example (b.3) at (5, 3, 7) inside Theorem D(1) and the primary-template example (b.4) at (5, 7, 3) outside gcd(N, 30) = 1.
- Section 1.2 (Theorem A summary): Explicitly stated 'non-scalar powers (g_p(t)^k notin C^x I_4)' when summarizing the rank->=2 bound for local puncture monodromy generators.
- Abstract (metadata.json and source manuscript): Streamlined inline formulas and repeated theorem details in the abstract (from 270 to 235 words) for readability while preserving all non-resonance, non-scalar power, and balanced vs. unbalanced Mumford-Tate scope qualifications.
title: Braid Monodromy Rigidity on One-Dimensional Symmetric Cyclic Prym Slices: Adjoint $\mathfrak{sl}_4$-Dichotomy, Ramanujan-Sum Trace Averages, and Length-Three Cyclotomic Separation
